problem: Insect-inspired CX/MB navigation models either ignore obstacles or use hardwired avoidance, and integrative models need a separate training phase on assumed-optimal routes, so they do not explain how routes are formed or refined. RL/SLAM point-goal agents need billions of training frames.
motivation: Ants learn continuously along their travelled routes and quickly optimise homing paths around obstacles, which is formally equivalent to visual point-goal navigation. A lightweight, mapless, online-learning model could match heavy RL agents without any pre-training.
key_idea: Combine a central-complex steering module (odometry-based goal direction) with a mushroom-body network that learns online, triggered by collisions and escapes, to associate views with obstacles and bias steering, plus selective STM/ITM/LTM memory consolidation gated by SPL.
insight: The strong goal-approach prior plus collision-triggered learning gives a high first-trial SR without training. Ablations show the reflexive collision pathway gives most of the gain over odometry-only (ΔSR 0.40, ΔSPL 0.20 in Habitat), and MB learning adds ΔSR 0.18 by solving episodes A2 fails. Selective consolidation prevents memory overload and over-caution (the OL variant is worse), and it also sustains performance under motor noise and bias in iGibson.
method: Visual preprocessing: front RGB is greyscaled, difference-of-Gaussians filtered and downsampled to 33x33 (1089 PNs).

MB associative learning: 1089 PN -> 32000 KC (fixed sparse binary random, k=320 winner-take-all) -> 2 MBONs (left/right). Only the KC-MBON weights are plastic, with a depression rule gated by DANs. Collisions trigger ipsilateral DANs and escape release triggers contralateral DANs, so MBON outputs encode left/right obstacle novelty.

CX steering: the desired rotation is target direction minus orientation plus MB modulation φ=π(zL−zR). The target is the goal direction, or a temporary escape tangent direction for τc after a collision. PI/odometry is abstracted.
Memory consolidation: weight changes are split into STM/ITM/LTM across trials. ITM is consolidated into LTM only if the trial SPL is at least the previous SPL. Learning ends when SPL drops.
Motor control: in Habitat, turn ±10° if |Δσ|≥10° else forward 0.25 m. In iGibson, (v,ω)=(cosΔσ, −sinΔσ).

Experiment protocol: 20 trials per episode with identical scene/start/goal, memory reset across episodes. Ablations A1 (odometry-only) and A2 (odometry+collision). Robustness tests add steering noise and bias in iGibson.

setting.backbone: Mushroom-body network (1089-32000-2, only KC-MBON weights plastic, online hetero-associative learning) + abstracted CX steering
setting.training_data: none (no pre-training; online learning during test trials, up to 500 frames in first trial)
setting.observation: front-facing monocular RGB (downsampled to 33x33 greyscale) + perfect GPS/compass odometry + collision signal/direction
setting.action_space: Habitat: discrete forward 0.25 m / turn ±10°; iGibson: continuous normalised linear and angular velocity
setting.privileged: Perfect odometry (GPS+compass) and collision information (not in standard task); 20 repeated trials per episode with learning carried across trials

numbers.eval_set_note: Actually Gibson 4+ val scenes (14 scenes); first trials averaged over 100 Habitat episodes (Gibson, not HM3D; paper text also mentions 93 standardised episodes for comparison)
numbers.extra: RGB only; uses GPS+compass and collision info; first trial of each episode; no separate training
numbers.evidence: Sec 3.1: 'SR=0.84 ... SPL=0.48' average of first trials across 100 Habitat episodes

numbers_note: Benchmark is Gibson PointNav (Habitat 2019 challenge, Gibson 4+ val); no canonical name for Gibson-PointNav split was mapped exactly, so bench label is imprecise. SR/SPL converted from 0.84/0.48. Other results (A1/A2, iGibson) appear only in figures.
results: On Habitat Gibson point-goal navigation, the first trial with no pre-training reaches SR 0.84 and SPL 0.48, comparable to or better than S1, S2, V1 and E1, though below V2, E2 and E3 which used billions of training frames. Learning across trials improves performance (~5 trials on average) and it stays robust under steering noise and bias in iGibson, where the odometry-collision ablation A2 fails.
limitations: Tested only in deterministic simulation with perfect odometry and collision sensing, with no real-robot validation.
First-trial paths are far from optimal (SPL 0.48), and selective consolidation can get stuck in local minima and risks over-cautious behaviour.
Comparison differs from the standard protocol: it uses collision data and repeated trials, and parameters are unoptimised.
